types.description: Alarm definitions evaluated against runtime data. The Condition expression references variables by their name (just the variable name; device-prefixed only when the variable's own name includes the device, e.g. via a {Device} token). The Actions field uses a strict JSON array-of-action-objects format documented in the field schema and must be preserved exactly.

Event definitions evaluated against runtime data. The Condition expression references variables by their name (just the variable name; device-prefixed only when the variable's own name includes the device, e.g. via a {Device} token). The Actions field uses a strict JSON array-of-action-objects format documented in the field schema and must be preserved exactly.

HMI pages. Only identity/access fields are managed here: Name, UserGroups, and LibraryPath. All visual and behavioral page properties (size, background, page script, zoom/pan, refresh time, base scale, replacers) are managed via UpdateDesignPage, and page HTML/graphical content is managed through the design tools.
notes: The list omits HTML content; pass id to GetConfigEntities to fetch one page including its full HTML and page script.
Page HTML is read-only here; edit graphical objects through the design tools.
On update, an omitted UserGroups or LibraryPath preserves its existing value.

types.description: Time-based schedules that execute actions when their on/off times are reached. Action fields use the strict JSON array-of-action-objects format documented in the field schema.
Value converters that translate raw variable values to display values and back.
Server-local variables that are not bound to an external communication device.
Data forwarders that push historic, alarm, event, audit trail, and electronic signature records to external targets. ForwardSignatures requires ForwardAudit.
User groups and their permission rights.

Server-side Python scripts triggered by actions, endpoint calls, or imported as modules by other scripts. Runnable scripts can be executed by name with the ExecutePythonScript tool to test them. A script can also write a document itself (fpdf, openpyxl and xlsxwriter ship with the product and import offline), which is the second way to produce a report; prefer a Reports entity with a declarative template whenever the output fits it, and keep this route for output that template cannot express. Ask the user which of the two they want when the request does not say; with no preference stated, build a Reports entity.

Report Designer reports. Each report holds a declarative template (TemplateJson) rendered to PDF (and Excel when ExcelCompatible) by the envision_report Python engine. Call GetReportTemplateSchema first for the exact TemplateJson structure; it also documents the inline {= python expression } form, which calculates a value in any text field, KPI binding, computed column or summary aggregate without a hook script. Enable gates scheduled/scripted execution; schedule a report with the 'Execute Report' action (Schedules/Alarms/Events, or on a page object where an operator fires it), render from a Python script with RunReport('Name', params={...}), or render immediately with the ExecuteReport tool. Run status surfaces on System.ReportStatus_<name>, where <name> is the report name with every character outside A-Za-z0-9_ replaced by '_'. A Reports entity is ONE of the two ways to produce a report document: the other is a PythonScripts entity that composes the file itself with the shipped fpdf/openpyxl/xlsxwriter libraries, which has no template, no period handling and no status variables, and is the right answer only for output this declarative template cannot express. Ask the user which of the two they want when the request does not say; with no preference stated, build a Reports entity.
notes: The list omits TemplateJson; pass id to GetConfigEntities to fetch one report including its full template.
TemplateJson must follow the schema from GetReportTemplateSchema; it is validated on every write.
An omitted/empty TemplateJson on insert creates a default single-page banded template; an omitted TemplateJson on update preserves the stored template.

OutputPath is the report's own destination folder (empty = the project folder's Reports subfolder). A destination that is given must be a FULL path such as D:\Reports or \\Server\Share\Reports; a relative path is rejected. It is a report field, not part of TemplateJson; an omitted OutputPath on update preserves the stored destination, an explicit empty string resets it to the default folder.

FileNamePattern names the rendered files without extension (empty = {Report.Name}_{Report.Day}). It must start with "{Report.Name}_", because the Files list identifies a report's own output by that prefix. It accepts the same placeholders as a text component plus a strftime spec on the typed period, for example {Report.Name}_{Report.Start:%Y%m%d_%H%M}_{Param.Line}. An omitted FileNamePattern on update preserves the stored pattern.

UserGroups lists the user groups allowed to run the report from a PAGE (the 'Execute Report' action on an object). Empty = Administrators only, and members of Administrators always pass. It gates that action only: this tool, the Reports page, the designer and RunReport() are administrator/automation paths, and an unattended Schedule/Alarm/Event action has no user to check.
Use ExecuteReport to render a report and get its output files.

types.description: Ethernet/IP communication devices, for Rockwell PLCs addressed by tag name. Create devices first, then create their variables as EthernetIPVariables. types.description: Variables under an Ethernet/IP device. Address is the controller tag name for LGX and MLGX800 (for example Pump1_Speed, MyUdt.Member or MyArray[2]), or the data file address for MLGX, SLC500 and PLC5 (for example N7:0). Type must match the tag's type in the controller: BOOL, BYTE, INT, UINT, WORD, DINT, UDINT, DWORD, REAL, LINT, ULINT, LREAL or STRING. A tag that cannot be read is reported per variable and does not take the rest of the device offline.

BACnet/IP communication devices. Create devices first, then create their variables as BacnetVariables. DeviceInstance is the BACnet device object instance (0-4194302); WritePriority (1-16, default 8) is the default BACnet write priority for the device's variables.
notes: Deleting a device also deletes all variables under it.

types.description: Variables under a BACnet/IP device. ObjectType is one of analog-input, analog-output, analog-value, binary-input, binary-output, binary-value, multi-state-input, multi-state-output, multi-state-value; ObjectInstance is 0-4194302; Property currently supports only present-value; WritePriority 0-16 where 0 inherits the device default.

IEC 60870-5-104 communication devices. Create devices first, then create their variables as Iec104Variables. CommonAddress is the common address of ASDU (1-65534) of the remote station; K/W and T0-T3 are the IEC 60870-5-104 protocol parameters; GiInterval is the periodic general interrogation interval in seconds (0 interrogates only on connection establishment); ClockSync sends a clock synchronization command after each connection establishment.
notes: Deleting a device also deletes all variables under it.

types.description: Variables under an IEC 60870-5-104 device. ObjectType is one of Single point (M_SP), Double point (M_DP), Step position (M_ST), Bitstring 32 bit (M_BO), Measured normalized (M_ME_NA), Measured scaled (M_ME_NB), Measured short float (M_ME_NC), Integrated total (M_IT), Single command (C_SC), Double command (C_DC), Regulating step command (C_RC), Setpoint normalized (C_SE_NA), Setpoint scaled (C_SE_NB), Setpoint short float (C_SE_NC); InformationObjectAddress is 1-16777215; Pulse sends single and double commands with the short-pulse qualifier instead of persistent output; CommandMode is one of Direct execute, Select before operate, Select before operate (operator) and applies to command object types only: the two select modes arm the point with a selection and execute it only after the remote station confirms that selection, and the operator mode splits those two steps across two operator actions on a page (the Select Command and Execute Command click actions, with Cancel Selection to release the point); it is a page-only flow, so an automated or API write to such a point still performs both steps in one call.

Mitsubishi MELSEC communication devices (MC protocol / SLMP 3E frame over TCP, default port 5007). Create devices first, then create their variables as MelsecVariables. Port is the TCP port of the SLMP connection configured in the PLC module parameters; AllowScanningBlocks reads consecutive device addresses together in batch requests; MaxBlockSizeAllowed is the maximum number of word devices read in one batch request (the SLMP 3E frame allows up to 960 words per request); AllowJumpingRegisters lets a batch request span unused device addresses between configured variables.
notes: Deleting a device also deletes all variables under it.

types.description: Generic EtherNet/IP devices addressed by CIP object path (explicit messaging over TCP, default port 44818). This is for standard CIP devices that have no controller tag namespace: drives, valve islands, IO blocks, sensors and third-party adapters. Use EthernetIPDevices instead for Rockwell PLCs (ControlLogix, CompactLogix, Micro800, MicroLogix, SLC500, PLC-5), which are addressed by symbolic tag name. Create devices first, then create their variables as EthernetIPGenericVariables. Port is the EtherNet/IP encapsulation port and is almost never changed from 44818. ScanRate is the milliseconds between scans; Timeout is applied per request rather than across the whole scan, so a device with many variables does not go offline as its variable count grows.
notes: Deleting a device also deletes all variables under it.

types.description: Variables under a generic EtherNet/IP device. Address is a CIP object path written as Class/Instance/Attribute, where each part is decimal or 0x-prefixed hexadecimal, for example 0x64/1/3, 100/1/3, or 0x04/100/3 to read the data attribute of an Assembly object. Instance 0 addresses the object class itself. Append a bit selector to read a single bit out of a packed attribute, for example 0x64/1/5.2 for bit 2; a bit selector requires Type BOOL. Type is one of BOOL, BYTE, INT, UINT, WORD, DINT, UDINT, DWORD, LINT, ULINT, REAL, LREAL or STRING. CIP transfers elementary types little-endian, so no byte or word swap setting is needed. BYTE covers an unsigned 8-bit attribute. STRING adapts to the length-prefix form the device uses, so the same Type reads a SHORT_STRING, a STRING or a fixed-length character array.

Beckhoff TwinCAT systems addressed over ADS. ADS is routed rather than point to point, so a device carries both an AmsNetId, which identifies the target runtime, and an IpAddress, which says where to reach it; the AmsNetId is shown in TwinCAT under SYSTEM and is not always the IP address with .1.1 appended. AmsPort selects the runtime: 851 is PLC runtime 1 on TwinCAT 3, 852 and 853 are runtimes 2 and 3, and 801 is PLC runtime 1 on TwinCAT 2. The PLC must also have a static route back to this server, added in TwinCAT under SYSTEM then Routes, using the local AmsNetId shown on the Beckhoff ADS Devices page; without it every request fails with target machine not found. No TwinCAT installation is required on the ENVISION server. Create devices first, then create their variables as BeckhoffAdsVariables. ScanRate is the milliseconds between scans; Timeout is applied per request rather than across the whole scan, so a device with many variables does not go offline as its variable count grows.

Variables under a Beckhoff ADS device. Address takes one of two forms, chosen automatically from the text. A PLC symbol path, for example MAIN.fbPump.rSpeed, GVL_IO.bAlarm or MAIN.aLevels[3], is resolved to a handle when the device connects and is what almost every project uses, because the symbol survives a recompile that moves the memory. A raw address written as IndexGroup:IndexOffset, for example 0x4020:12 for %MB12 or 0x4021:100 for memory bit 100, reaches areas that publish no symbol; each part is decimal or 0x-prefixed hexadecimal. A colon is the discriminator, since symbol paths cannot contain one. IndexGroup 0x4021 addresses a single memory bit and requires Type BOOL. Type is one of BOOL, BYTE, INT, UINT, WORD, DINT, UDINT, DWORD, LINT, ULINT, REAL, LREAL or STRING; TwinCAT uses the IEC 61131-3 types directly, so the name matches the PLC declaration. ADS transfers elementary types little-endian, so no byte or word swap setting is needed. All points of a device are read in a single ADS sum command per scan, whichever address form they use.

Variables under a Mitsubishi MELSEC device. Address is a MELSEC device address in GX Works3 notation, for example D100, W1A0, R200, SD210 (word devices), M100, B1F, SM400 (bit devices) or X17, Y10 (octal, iQ-F numbering). types.description: Identities of ENVISION's own embedded MQTT broker, with the topic access control list of each identity nested in the Acls field. Unrelated to MqttClients: those are outbound connections to external brokers, these are the accounts external clients use to connect to ENVISION. The broker itself is switched on and configured through the EnableMqttBroker, MqttBrokerPort, MqttBrokerTlsEnabled, MqttBrokerTlsPort, MqttBrokerCertificateName, MqttBrokerAllowAnonymous, MqttBrokerEnforceTopicAcl and MqttBrokerLogEntries parameters.

TopicFilter is an MQTT topic filter and may use wildcards: '+' matches one level and must occupy a whole level, '#' matches the remaining levels and must be the last level (for example plant/+/temperature or devices/site1/#).

Password is write-only. It is stored as a salted hash and is never returned by GET. Omit it on update to keep the current password; it is required on create.

'Anonymous' is a reserved identity that cannot be created, renamed or deleted and carries no username or password. Its rules apply to clients that connect without credentials while MqttBrokerAllowAnonymous is enabled.
Changes apply to connected clients immediately without restarting the broker; the edited identity's own sessions are disconnected so it reconnects under the new rules.

UDT (User Defined Type) definitions: reusable, parameterized type templates whose variable/alarm/event members carry {Token} placeholders. A definition is inert; UdtInstances reference it, and a PUSH (PushUdtInstances) is the single operation that materializes anything - creating or editing definitions and instances only stages configuration. Members are nested (Parameters, VariableMembers, AlarmMembers, EventMembers) and the whole definition is created or replaced atomically. A parameter is typed Text, Number or Device, and a Device parameter holds a device NAME (any protocol, or the reserved name Local). Each variable member names its OWN target device in DeviceName, so one definition can span several devices and protocols. The built-in tokens {Instance} and {Asset} are always available, plus {Index} on array members only (see the ARRAY MEMBERS note). There is no built-in {Device} token and no privileged parameter name: a Device parameter may be called anything, and a member with an EMPTY DeviceName uses the type's single Device-typed parameter, resolved by TYPE - which is an error when the type declares none or several, so those types must name the parameter on the member. Saving a definition never changes materialized rows: instances become Outdated and are updated only through an explicit push (PreviewUdtPush/PushUdtInstances).
notes: The list is a SUMMARY and is the exact answer of GET /API/Config/UdtDefinitions?summary=true, NOT of the bare GET (which defaults to summary=false and inlines every member): each type reports its name, description, version, bound symbol masters, base definition name, slot count, instance/outdated counts and how many parameters and variable/alarm/event/script members it has, but not the members themselves. Pass id to GetConfigEntities to fetch ONE definition in full - do that before an update, because an update replaces the whole member set.
Version and VersionDateTime are stamped by the server on every save and are ignored on input.
Nested member lists replace the definition's whole member set on update: send every member that should remain.
Members are matched by natural key on update (parameter/variable Name, alarm/event Condition template); renaming a key materializes as delete+add on the next push.

The ORDER of each member array is the display order and is stored as such - there is no reorder endpoint and no order field on the wire. Re-sending the members in a different order is how the order is changed. Order is cosmetic: it is excluded from the version hash, so it never flips an instance between Synced and Outdated.

Alarm and event members carry Actions, the same JSON array of action objects the Alarms and Events pages use. A member's actions are a TEMPLATE: they may contain {Instance}, {Asset} and parameter tokens (a Device-typed parameter token, whatever the parameter is named, included), which resolve at push, and the resolved action is validated then. Call GetConfigEntityTypeSchema and read the itemSchema of alarmMembers/eventMembers for the exact action format.

TARGET DEVICES are per MEMBER. Declare a Device-typed parameter under any name you like and point each variable member's DeviceName at it, e.g. "{Drive}" or "{PowerMeter}"; a literal device name is also allowed, and the reserved name Local materializes the member into LocalVariables. An EMPTY DeviceName means the type's SINGLE Device-typed parameter, resolved by TYPE and not by any privileged name - so a type declaring exactly one device parameter needs no wiring, while a type declaring none or several rejects an empty DeviceName (errorKey UdtMemberDeviceAmbiguous) and each member must say which parameter it uses. Device names are globally unique across every protocol, so the resolved name identifies both the device and its protocol - and that is what selects which of the member's per-protocol field groups (ModbusTcp*, OpcUa*, S7*, Dnp3*, ...) is used and which variable table the row lands in. Declaring two Device parameters lets one instance mix, for example, polled drive points with local setpoints or a second meter's registers.

NO TOKEN IS PRIVILEGED inside a definition, {Device} included: in a member name, address, condition, message, action or symbol mapping it is an ordinary parameter reference that resolves if and only if the type declares a parameter with that name, exactly like {Drive} or {PowerMeter}. Materialized names are FULLY resolved (a member on {PLC} named {PLC}.{Instance}_Run materializes as e.g. PLC2.Pump1_Run), so names and alarm/event conditions always agree - name the variable after the parameter that supplies its device if it should read as that device's point. Renaming a device does NOT rename materialized variable names; use the Cross Reference tool to bulk-repair references after a device rename, the same as for hand-written variables.

ARRAY MEMBERS: a variable, alarm or event member with a non-empty ArrayCount (a number or a parameter token like {StageCount}, 1-512 resolved) materializes one row per element. The member's Name/Condition must contain the built-in {Index} token, which resolves per element to ArrayStart + element number (ArrayStart empty = 0). Addresses may compute per element with {= arithmetic }, e.g. %MW{= {BaseAddress} + {Index} * 2 }. Resizing outdates instances; a push adds/removes tail elements while existing elements keep their row identity.
A definition with instances cannot be deleted; delete or detach the instances first.

Move types between projects with ExportUdtTypes / ImportUdtTypes: the export is a version-stamped file (schemaVersion = the database user_version) and import refuses a file newer than this app, upgrades an older one, skips existing names unless overwrite=true, and warns (not fails) when a type's group symbol master is absent.

FULL LIFECYCLE of a UDT type: 1) define it here (members/parameters, optional Symbols bindings). 2) create instances (insert on UdtInstances; Asset decides the identity, ParameterValues supply the devices) - this only STAGES them, state NotMaterialized, no rows exist yet. 3) PreviewUdtPush, then PushUdtInstances: the push is the single delivery gate that creates/updates the materialized variable/alarm/event rows (adopt=true takes over matching unmanaged rows instead of colliding). 4) later definition or instance edits stage again (state Outdated) and the next push delivers them. 5) DetachUdtInstances releases rows as hand-editable (one-way); deleting an instance removes it AND its rows immediately - delete is the one operation that does not wait for a push.

GRAPHICS are a separate surface: the Symbols binding here names one or more group symbol masters, each with its own replacer mapping, but placing a symbol on a page for an instance is a DESIGN operation - use CreateUdtSymbol (design tools) once per master you want placed, and PushUdtInstances re-stamps each placed symbol's mapped replacers using the mapping of the master it was placed from.

DERIVATION (composition): BaseDefinition names the type this one derives from (single inheritance, by name, empty = none). The base's parameters and members are part of this type's EFFECTIVE definition and are NOT repeated in the authored member lists; a derived type may ADD members and parameters, may redeclare a base parameter to change its DEFAULT only (same Type), and may not redefine a base member. Editing a base flags the instances of every deriving type Outdated - deliver with the ordinary push.

CONTAINMENT (composition): Slots declares contained sub-types - each slot names an inner definition and materializes its effective members once per instance, parameterized by ParameterMapping (inner parameter name -> token expression in THIS type's namespace; an omitted inner parameter uses its own default; mapping a Device-typed inner parameter puts the slot on its own device). Inside slot members {Slot} is the slot name and {SlotPath} the dotted path; when two or more slots share one definition, that definition's member names must contain {Slot} or {SlotPath}. A slot's IncludeWhen (outer namespace) excludes the whole slot for an instance.

The GET adds a READ-ONLY effective projection: EffectiveParameters and EffectiveVariableMembers/EffectiveAlarmMembers/EffectiveEventMembers list what an instance actually materializes (Origin: Own | Inherited | Slot, plus SlotPath, SourceDefinition and MemberId). NEVER merge these into the authored VariableMembers/AlarmMembers/EventMembers on an update - the authored lists remain this type's OWN members only, and round-tripping an inherited member into them forks the base silently.
A definition referenced as a base or slot by another definition cannot be deleted (UdtDefinitionInUseByType); type export auto-includes the transitive base/slot closure so the file stays importable.

TYPE-OWNED LOGIC: ScriptMembers carry Python every instance runs. The BODY is shared (not token-substituted) and reads per-instance values with GetParam('Instance'), GetParam('Asset'), GetParam('Slot'), GetParam('SlotPath') and every parameter by name; the TRIGGER fields are tokenized per instance - Interval (ms, periodic), RunWhen (runs once on the false-to-true edge of the condition; a condition already standing true when the instance is pushed, when the application starts or after a promotion has shown no edge and does NOT run - use RunAtStartup for that; nothing is written to the event history) and RunAtStartup (application start and promotion to primary). The push materializes the state (body + resolved ctx + triggers) per instance, so logic changes stage and deliver exactly like variable changes; per-instance health surfaces on System.PythonStatus_<instance>.<script> / System.PythonMsg_<instance>.<script>.

types.description: Instances of a UdtDefinition. Creating or editing an instance STAGES configuration only - nothing is materialized until a PUSH (PushUdtInstances), the single audited delivery gate, creates or updates its real variable/alarm/event rows (provenance-stamped and locked against direct edits). Each instance reports State: NotMaterialized (staged only, no rows exist yet), Outdated (rows exist but a push would change them - the definition moved, edits were staged, or the identity moved with the tree) or Synced (a push would change nothing); Outdated=true is shorthand for State!=Synced. The instance NAME is its identity and is COMPOSED by the server: the Asset path with dots plus the leaf name sent in Name, e.g. Asset "WTP/Line2/Pumps" + Name "Pump1" -> "WTP.Line2.Pumps.Pump1" (send the leaf or the full form; both store the same). The leaf only has to be unique within its node, and the identity follows the tree: renaming or moving a node re-composes it. The {Instance} token resolves to the LEAF. An instance carries NO device of its own: devices are ordinary ParameterValues entries for the definition's Device-typed parameters (any protocol, or the reserved name Local), and each variable member picks the one its DeviceName points at, so one instance can span several devices, protocols and variable tables. ParameterValues holds only explicitly set values; a missing parameter inherits the definition default on every push. A successful create/update may return warnings: they are the findings the NEXT PUSH would report (unknown device, name collision) - fix and push, or push with adopt.
notes: CREATE STAGES, PUSH MATERIALIZES. A new instance has State NotMaterialized and owns no rows until PushUdtInstances delivers it; a push of nothing but NotMaterialized instances needs no reason (it is the initial create), while a push touching materialized instances requires one. Materializing onto existing unmanaged rows: push with adopt=true (the migration path from hand-written rows; rows managed by ANOTHER instance always block).

EDIT STAGES TOO: updating name, asset or parameter values changes configuration only, sets State Outdated, and the materialized rows plus any placed symbols stay exactly as the last push left them until the next push delivers everything at once. Deleting is the exception and is immediate: it removes the instance AND its materialized rows now (a NotMaterialized instance is just a row delete). Detaching (DetachUdtInstances) instead strips provenance so the rows survive as ordinary hand-editable rows.

The DEFINITION of an existing instance cannot be changed; delete and recreate the instance instead. Its DEVICES can: stage a new value for a Device-typed parameter and the NEXT PUSH moves the materialized rows - in place when the new device speaks the same protocol, otherwise as a delete on the old device plus an add on the new one, which gives the row a new id but keeps its trend history (the historian keys on the variable name). Rows must not collide with existing ones on the new device; the create/update warnings and PreviewUdtPush both report a collision before anything is written.
A device cannot be deleted while it still carries rows materialized by a UDT instance. Delete or detach the instance, or point the member(s) at another device, first.
Asset is the tree node path (e.g. Site/Line A); missing segments are created automatically.

SortOrder is the display order among the instances attached to the same asset node; 0 means unordered and falls back to sorting by name, so a project that has never been reordered stays alphabetical. It is honoured on create and on project import, but IGNORED on update: reorder with ReorderUdtInstances ([{Id, SortOrder}]), which writes only the order and leaves the materialized rows and the Synced/Outdated state untouched. Ties fall back to the name sort, so renumber a whole node's instances (0..n-1) rather than a single row.

BULK CREATE: there is no bulk-by-count endpoint - the GUI's {N} name pattern is expanded client-side into individual instances. To create many instances at once from MCP, POST a LIST of instance objects to this endpoint, each with its own Name and ParameterValues, including its own device name(s) in the Device-typed parameters (that is how one type fans out over a fleet: same definition, one instance per device). To step a per-instance value (typically a protocol address base), a ParameterValues value may be a compute expression {= arithmetic } using digits and + - * / ( ) and other parameter tokens; the expression TEXT stays on the instance and is re-evaluated on every push; only its result reaches the materialized rows, e.g. a 'Base register' parameter = "{= 3000 + (4 - 1) * 100 }" for the 4th instance. This is the same mechanism a definition member address uses with {Index} (see the UdtDefinitions ARRAY MEMBERS note); anything left after substitution that is not plain arithmetic fails the plan rather than passing through.

Lifecycle tools around an instance: PreviewUdtPush (dry-run diff, also with adopt=true) + PushUdtInstances (materialize staged state; reason required unless every pushed instance is new; adopt=true takes over matching unmanaged rows), DetachUdtInstances (release rows, one-way), ReorderUdtInstances (display order), GetUdtInstanceRows (what an instance actually materialized, across every protocol table). Placing the instance's group symbol on a page is a DESIGN operation - CreateUdtSymbol.

types.description: Asset Manager tree nodes (plant hierarchy). ParentId 0 is the root level. Each node's full path (e.g. Site/Line A/Pumps) is materialized into the flat Asset text field of attached variables, alarms, events, schedules and Python scripts, so the viewers filter by plain path prefix. Renaming or moving a node rewrites the Asset value of every row carrying an affected path, and RE-COMPOSES the identity of every UDT instance attached at or below it (an instance's Name IS its dotted asset path plus leaf), leaving those instances Outdated until their next push re-points their placed symbols and any {Asset}-using conditions.
notes: A node with child nodes or attached UDT instances cannot be deleted.
Sibling names must be unique; a node name is a single path segment and cannot contain '/'.

SortOrder is the display order among sibling nodes (0 = unordered, falls back to name). Set it directly on update, or reorder a whole sibling set at once with ReorderAssets (an ordered id list the server renumbers by position). A pure reorder changes no paths.

Before renaming or re-parenting a node, call GetAssetAttachedCounts to see how many rows carry this node's own path (variables, alarms, events, schedules and Python scripts); a rename also rewrites the whole SUBTREE, so for a node with children the count understates the effect; a reorder does not rewrite paths.

An asset node carries no geographic position. A symbol placed on a Map design object holds its own position: either the name of one variable whose value is "lat,lon" (for example 51.2194,4.4025), or a fixed longitude and latitude. Set it with the map child tools, not here.
